title: Sparks and Embers
description: Sparks and embers are incandescent particles thrown by welding, fire, grinding, or a cigarette: orange weather with short trajectories. They are burning matter; backlight is optional because they are their own small keys.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A welder writes a fountain. A collapsing floor throws embers that hang, then die.
Industry or apocalypse in the air. Unlike dust, these specks have temperature and a brief life.

Use it when the air should be dangerous or industrial: a foundry, a burning street, a cigarette in a dark booth (embers, not a fountain). It is the wrong tool when the specks are cold (Dust Motes, Snow).

It is the wrong tool when the glow is only a warm key on a face with no particles: that is Candlelight or firelight without weather. If the particles are large, slow, and white, you probably asked for snow.
If they never fall, you asked for hanging dust.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Give them a source (welder, angle grinder, timber, cigarette). Let gravity and heat dictate: sparks drop and bounce; embers can loft and drift.
Expose for the particle without losing the face entirely, or accept silhouettes. A dark surround makes them read.
Prompt: sparks or embers around [Subject], welding, fire, cigarettes, orange particles as weather.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for a night burn, a factory, a ruined city, a match. Do not sprinkle orange specks on a pastoral wide with no fire.
Particles need a reason.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Candlelight is a warm, flickering key. Sparks are the particles.
Volumetric Light is a shaft; sparks can cross it but are not the shaft. Dust Motes are cold and slow in a beam.
Snow is cold and accumulates. Sparks die in the air.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Blade Runner 2049 throws orange particles as industrial weather. The Dark Knight Rises uses fire and debris as airborne specks in night action.
Use source plus trajectory, not a spark overlay on a clean street.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Sparks or embers around [Subject], welding, fire, cigarettes, orange particles as weather. Name the source, color (white-orange to dull red), trajectory (fountain versus lofted drift), and a dark surround.
For video, short-lived particles with gravity; no snow, no cigarette smoke unless you also want smoke.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Dust Motes tinted orange, or Snow. The tell: specks hang forever, accumulate on the ground as white, or have no welder or fire.
The fix: a hot source, brief trajectories, self-luminous particles, dark air.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Sparks and Embers in film?
Sparks and embers are burning particles in the air, thrown by welding, fire, or a cigarette. They light themselves, follow short trajectories, and die.
Sparks and Embers vs Dust Motes
Dust motes are cold specks in a shaft of light. Sparks are incandescent and come from a hot source. One is time in a closed room; the other is industry or fire.
When should I use Sparks and Embers?
Use them when the air should carry heat: welding, collapse, a cigarette coal. Do not sprinkle orange dots on a scene with no fire.
How do I prompt Sparks and Embers for AI image or video?
Name the hot source and the trajectories. Example: sparks or embers around [Subject], welding, fire, cigarettes, orange particles as weather. Dark surround, gravity, no snow.
